question: Why is `track` required in `@for`?
options: It identifies items so Angular can reuse and move DOM nodes instead of recreating them
It is only used by the dev tools
explanation: With a stable key Angular knows which item each DOM node belongs to, which keeps updates fast and preserves element state like focus or input text.

question: Which is the modern equivalent of `<li *ngFor="let x of list; let i = index">`?
options:
`@for (x of list; track x; let i = $index) {
  • …
    • }`
explanation: `@for` requires a `track` expression; the index is the implicit `$index` variable, optionally aliased with `let`.

question: What happens in `@switch` when two `@case` blocks follow each other without `break`?
options: Execution falls through to the next case
Only the matching case renders; there is no fall-through
explanation: Template `@switch` has no fall-through and no `break`: exactly one matching `@case` (or `@default`) renders.
